summary: Full end-to-end verification of TradingView webhook -> Discord signal delivery pipeline. Wrote a new pytest suite (test_tradingview_webhook_pipeline.py) covering buy/sell paths, signal persistence with correct entry/stop/tp1/tp2 (-8/+10/+20), duplicate suppression within 3-min window, kill-switch block+restore, Pine script v3 endpoint (alertcondition + JSON messages + https webhook URL), latency (<2s avg), and Discord delivery verification via backend logs. All 8 new tests pass. Also ran the existing regression suites test_signal_engine.py + test_signal_engine_v2.py: 47/47 pass. Kill switch confirmed OFF at end. Zero 'Discord send failed' entries in backend logs. Latency observed ~200-400ms per POST.

minor.issue: Duplicate suppression is per (symbol,side) within 3min but queries status:'active' with no upper bound; signals never auto-transition out of 'active', so a single active long can block ALL long webhooks for 3 min regardless of price. Currently working as designed but consider closing old signals when a new one arrives to keep the flow responsive.

Response key is 'pine_script' (snake_case) while other similar endpoints use camelCase. Cosmetic — not a bug. Webhook host in instructions is derived from request.headers Host, which for the ingress resolves to the emergentcf.cloud host rather than REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL public host. Users will still be able to POST to it, but a mismatch with the branded public URL could surprise them.
signal_engine_state['errors'] is incremented on duplicate hits. Semantically a duplicate is not an error; this inflates the error rate used by the auto kill-switch (>5% threshold) in /system/health.

action_items: Consider decoupling duplicate detection from status: use created_at only (any signal in last N minutes), or explicitly close active signals after TP/SL/timeout so duplicate window is meaningful.
Do not increment signal_engine_state['errors'] on duplicate suppression — dedup hits are expected traffic and should not degrade the auto-kill-switch health metric.
Optional: return derived https URL from REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL (or an env var PUBLIC_APP_URL) in pinescript webhook_instructions so the URL shown to users matches the branded domain.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 2500+ lines — should be split into routers (signals, webhook, operator, checkout, etc.).
send_discord_signal creates a new httpx.AsyncClient per call; reuse a shared client for lower latency/connection reuse.
check_duplicate_signal filters by status:'active' but nothing marks signals inactive automatically; combined with 3-min window this is fragile.
receive_tradingview_webhook payload accepts price as string then floats it without validation — a bad payload will raise ValueError -> 500. Wrap in try/except and return 400.
test_credentials: not needed; endpoints under test are unauthenticated
seed_data_creation: Created ~5 signal documents in db.signals via webhook. Cleared prior 'active' signals to 'closed_by_test' to allow duplicate-suppression test to run deterministically.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Pipeline verified end-to-end. Kill switch is OFF. New regression file at /app/backend/tests/test_tradingview_webhook_pipeline.py — export REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL before running. To rerun cleanly, the fixture auto-closes prior active signals via direct MongoDB access using MONGO_URL/DB_NAME from /app/backend/.env.
rca of the issue: Initial run of the new tests appeared to fail with status:'duplicate' because prior iterations left long signals in status:'active'; the webhook's dedup check (status:active + last 3 min) blocked new longs. Root cause: signals never transition out of 'active'. Mitigation in tests: reset active->closed_by_test in a module fixture. Product-side mitigation recommended in action_items.
